$comment: Passenger demand profiles by building type. See docs/03-traffic-and-statistics.md.

arrivalProcess.$comment: Passengers arrive in groups, not singly. Batch size materially changes loading and stop patterns.

profiles.name: Prestige office
profiles.blurb: The morning crush at a headline address: nearly everyone pours in through the lobby at once, and the bank is judged on how fast that queue clears.

profiles.name: Standard office
profiles.blurb: An ordinary office morning: a steady stream in through the lobby, with light floor-to-floor errands once people are at their desks.

profiles.name: Residential
profiles.blurb: Apartment mornings run downward — residents leave through the lobby, and families ride together, so groups are larger. Evenings invert to an up-peak.
profiles.$comment: PM inverts to up-peak. Larger batches: families travel together.

profiles.name: Hotel
profiles.blurb: Hotel demand runs both ways all day: guests come and go while housekeeping and room service move between floors, with no single dominant direction.

demandTemplates.$comment: Single long run. Incompatible with confidence intervals across replications because waiting times within one run are correlated. Supported for cross-checking only.

demandTemplates.name: CIBSE Guide D lunch two-way template
demandTemplates.shape: the rise-and-fall intensity, with the directional mix swinging from outgoing-dominant to incoming-dominant across the period
demandTemplates.$comment: The lunch mixed peak: occupants ride down to the terminal to leave the building, and later ride up again on their return, so the SAME period is outgoing-dominant early and incoming-dominant late. CITED: the period's mix is 45% incoming / 45% outgoing / 10% interfloor (CIBSE Guide D, 2010, carried into 2020; the same split is what BCO Guide to Specification 2014 pairs with a 13%/5min lunchtime two-way demand). Alternatives in the literature are 40/40/20 (Barney 2003a) and 42/42/16 (BCO 2009); the CIBSE figure is taken because Guide D is this project's primary reference. DERIVED, and not quoted from any table: the two endpoints. At the instant the period opens nobody has returned yet, so incoming is 0; interfloor is held at the cited 10% throughout; the mix is linear in time and symmetric about the midpoint, so its time-average is (start+end)/2 = 45/45/10 exactly -- the cited figure is REPRODUCED by the endpoints rather than assumed beside them. NOT CITED, and inherited rather than invented: every geometric number here. durationMin, the 5-minute hold and the zero baseline are the rise-and-fall record's own, so this template adds no uncited duration. LIMITATION: an endpoint of exactly 0 incoming is the widest arc consistent with the cited mean, and a measured building's arc is smoother at its ends; `traffic.lunchTwoWay.mixAmplitude` scales the arc about that mean, and 0 collapses it to a flat 45/45/10 at identical total demand.

passengerMass.$comment: Drives the load sensor. Must be a distribution, not a constant, or the load sensor has nothing to measure.
